text: Large Language Models, or LLMs, are computer programs that understand and generate human language. They work by predicting the next word in a sentence, based on patterns learned from huge amounts of text. This training data includes books, websites, and articles. Users can get better results by writing clear prompts, which is called prompt engineering. LLMs are good at tasks like answering questions, summarising texts, and translating languages. However, they have limits. They can make mistakes, sometimes invent false information, and they do not truly understand meaning the way humans do.
